title: Console walkthrough - usage analytics & cost breakdown
summary: Redwood AE/SE walk through the Console focusing on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and token-level cost breakdowns. Customer (Atlas Health) asks about cost allocation, multi-team routing, and private deployment / compliance requirements. Agreed next steps: send detailed pricing sheet, share SOC2/HIPAA notes, schedule a short pilot kick-off next week with sample routing preset.
transcript:
Header: 2025-05-08 16:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Avery Chen, Marcus Hale (Redwood) — Priya Singh, Liam O'Connor, Jasmin Patel (Atlas Health)

00:00 Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're gonna do a quick console walkthrough today focused on usage analytics and per-route cost breakdown, and then leave time for questions. Marcus and I are on deck.
00:12 Priya Singh: Thanks — appreciate it. We got about 45 minutes. We mostly want to see how we'd attribute egress to different products and cost per feature.
00:22 Marcus Hale: Great. I'll share my screen. (screen share noise) Alright, you should see the Redwood Console. Sorry if the resolution's a bit low, I'm on a hotspot.
00:35 Marcus Hale: Top-left you can see the global usage dashboard — total tokens, requests per minute, 95th latency, and spend over time. You can change the window, let's pick last 30 days.
00:48 Liam O'Connor: That spend number — is that raw cloud spend or Redwood-billed cost? We need something that maps to internal chargeback.
00:57 Marcus Hale: Good question. The default is Redwood's normalized cost model — it maps GPU runtime, instance type, and model variant into a unit cost per token. You can export the raw metrics and also the normalized cost. We do have a per-tenant and per-route breakdown which is what helps with chargeback.
01:12 Priya Singh: Show the per-route please.
01:15 Marcus Hale: Sure. Switching to Routes view. Here are routes for your account: patient-summary (high volume), triage-chat (burst), and research-embeddings. Each route has its own throughput, avg latency, and cost per 1k tokens.
01:30 Marcus Hale: Notice the token cost column — that's where we show the token-level microbilling. For example, patient-summary is 0.9 units per 1k tokens because it's hitting a larger model with KV cache misses.
01:44 Jasmin Patel: KV cache misses? Do we have control over caching TTLs or prefix cache?
01:49 Marcus Hale: Yes — on the route config you can toggle prefix caching, set TTL, and we surface cache hit rate in the dashboard. High hit rate drops cost a lot.
01:58 Priya Singh: Can you drill into a single route? We want to understand spikes and what caused them.
02:03 Marcus Hale: Absolutely. Clicking into patient-summary. You get a timeline of requests, per-minute latency, and a small table of exemplar requests. There are filters by model version, sequence length bucket, and time of day.
02:15 Marcus Hale: For the spike last Tuesday at 14:30 you can see sequence length jumped — probably because longer patient histories were included — and that correlates with a 3x cost delta.
02:28 Liam O'Connor: Can we tag requests by team or product? So billing is split across groups?
02:33 Marcus Hale: Yes — we support metadata tagging on requests, and tags show up in the analytics as first-class filters. You can also define aggregation rules to allocate cost to teams automatically.
02:44 Priya Singh: How about model routing? If we want lower cost during peak, can we route to a cheaper model automatically?
02:51 Marcus Hale: That's part of Smart Routing. You can add a policy on the route: prefer low-cost model for non-critical requests, fallback to higher-quality model on errors or if latency SLOs aren't met. We can demo a canary routing after the call as part of a pilot.
03:06 Jasmin Patel: From a quality perspective, how do you measure regressions if we switch models?
03:10 Marcus Hale: We tie evals to route versions — you upload a test set, and the console shows regression/delta metrics over time (BLEU-ish for specific tasks or similarity scores for embeddings).
03:22 Priya Singh: Security — we are a health company. HIPAA concerns. Can you walk through audit logs and SSO?
03:29 Avery Chen: Sure — quick note I'm the AE here, Marcus is our SE. For HIPAA folks we provide a Private deployment option; but from a Console standpoint we surface audit logs for each request, KMS-encrypted customer keys, and support SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning. We'll share the SOC2 and HIPAA posture docs after.
03:48 Priya Singh: Do audit logs include redacted request bodies or full payloads?
03:53 Marcus Hale: You can configure retention and redaction policies. By default we store metadata and pointers; full request bodies can be encrypted and stored for configured retention windows, or routed to customer-managed storage for Private deployments.
04:06 Liam O'Connor: What about on-prem? Latency and data residency are big for us.
04:11 Avery Chen: We have Redwood Private which can run in your VPC or on-prem. The Console still connects to your control plane, or you can run a fully air-gapped variant. For this demo we're on hosted, but pilot options include Dedicated or Private.
04:26 Jasmin Patel: Let's get back to cost. Can you show an example CSV export for chargeback?
04:31 Marcus Hale: Exporting now — CSV includes timestamp, route, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, normalized_cost_usd, tags. You can hook it into Snowflake or BigQuery via our integrations.
04:44 Priya Singh: Nice. That normalized_cost_usd — what's the unit? I want to understand how it maps to our SRE budget.
04:52 Marcus Hale: That is an estimate built from instance mix and quantization profile. For Dedicated or Private you'll get a different mapping — in Dedicated we show committed hours amortized across tokens. We can add a column for amortized infra if you need.
05:08 Liam O'Connor: Any way to see per-model token breakdown? Like how many tokens were context vs generated?
05:14 Marcus Hale: Yes — the transcript shows input_tokens and output_tokens. The per-route table splits those. We also surface KV cache hits separately so you can see effective tokens served from cache.
05:26 Priya Singh: Do you support retroactive tagging — if we add tags later, can we re-allocate historic cost?
05:31 Marcus Hale: You can backfill tags in the analytics engine, yes. The UI has a mapping tool for rule-based backfill.
05:40 Priya Singh: Okay, good.
05:42 Marcus Hale: Quick demo of the cost heatmap — this shows cost per route by hour. Darker blocks are expensive. You can click a block to see all requests in that hour.
05:53 Jasmin Patel: Do you have alerting on cost anomalies?
05:56 Marcus Hale: Yup, set threshold alerts — e.g., sudden token increase or cost spike. We also provide automated suggestions in Redwood Optimize — like enable prefix caching or change quantization for specific routes.
06:10 Priya Singh: What's the Optimize recommendation fidelity? We tried heuristics in-house and they often suggest things that break quality.
06:18 Marcus Hale: Optimize recommendations are ranked by predicted cost savings and estimated quality delta. You can preview the expected impact on an eval set. We don't auto-apply without explicit approval.
06:29 Liam O'Connor: Any examples of savings?
06:32 Marcus Hale: For a customer with heavy embedding traffic, enabling batching + int8 quantized model saved ~42% on tokens cost; for a chat product, prefix caching saved up to 60% on repeated system prompts.
06:45 Priya Singh: For compliance, do you retain prompts? We try to avoid storing PHI.
06:50 Marcus Hale: You can redact or avoid storing request bodies. For workflows that need PHI, Private deployment with customer-managed storage is recommended.
06:58 Priya Singh: Do you provide a per-route SLA or is it per-account?
07:02 Avery Chen: For Dedicated customers we offer SLA-backed latency and availability, and per-route SLOs can be configured. Hosted has best-effort SLOs with region fallbacks.
07:14 Jasmin Patel: Can we simulate load to see how cost scales?
07:18 Marcus Hale: We have a load-test harness we can run in a pilot. We'll run a small synthetic workload against patient-summary to show cost scaling and latency under load.
07:28 Priya Singh: Walk me through the steps to set up a pilot.
07:31 Avery Chen: Typical pilot: 2-week window, route mirroring, run load tests, capture analytics, share results and recommendations. We'll provide a pilot pricing credit and a short PO if you want Dedicated evaluation.
07:44 Liam O'Connor: Who signs the pilot PO? Legal or procurement?
07:47 Priya Singh: Procurement. We'll loop them in if the pilot looks good.
07:51 Marcus Hale: Back to the console — here's an example of a per-route policy: threshold-based fallback. If p95 latency > 400ms then route to cheaper model or fall back to cached answer.
08:05 Jasmin Patel: Does fallback affect consistency of outputs? We need identical results for some research queries.
08:12 Marcus Hale: Fallbacks are opt-in per route and annotated in the trace logs so you can filter requests that hit fallback. For strict consistency you can pin routes to a single model and disable fallback.
08:24 Priya Singh: This is helpful. Can I see the audit log sample?
08:27 Marcus Hale: (scrolling) The audit view shows action, actor, resource, timestamp. For request-level tracing we show request_id, route, model_version, tokens_in/out, processing_time, and any fallback events.
08:42 Priya Singh: Perfect.
08:44 Avery Chen: Quick pause — any other blocking questions on cost or the console?
08:48 Priya Singh: One more — pricing tiers. How granular are the hosted pricing tiers and do you offer committed discounts?
08:55 Avery Chen: Hosted is usage-based; we offer committed commitments for Dedicated. For larger accounts we do volume discounts and committed spend; we'll include a pricing sheet with dedicated pilot terms.
09:07 Liam O'Connor: Can you share the mapping of model variants to cost? So our finance team can forecast.
09:12 Marcus Hale: Yes — we'll give you the model catalog with perf profiles and normalized cost per 1k tokens. It's in the docs and we'll attach a spreadsheet.
09:20 Priya Singh: Are there any hidden costs — egress, storage, logs?
09:24 Avery Chen: We break out infra amortization, storage, and logs. For hosted, storage and logs are included up to a retention limit; beyond that there's an add-on. We'll be explicit in the cost sheet.
09:36 Jasmin Patel: Okay.
09:38 Marcus Hale: Wrapping up the demo — here's the export and the Optimize suggestions pane. If you click a suggestion you can preview on sample traffic.
09:48 Priya Singh: That preview is useful.
09:50 Avery Chen: Alright, let's do a quick recap and next steps.
09:54 Priya Singh: Sounds good.
10:00 Avery Chen: Next steps: we'll send the pricing sheet and SOC2/HIPAA notes; Marcus will schedule a pilot kick-off and run the load-test; Jasmin, you'll share a small eval set so the Optimize recommendations can be measured.
10:14 Priya Singh: Yep. Also please include the model catalog spreadsheet and mapping to normalized cost.
10:20 Avery Chen: Noted. Any blockers on timelines?
10:23 Jasmin Patel: We can start next Monday for the pilot.
10:26 Avery Chen: Great. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.
10:31 Liam O'Connor: Thanks all.
10:33 Avery Chen: Bye.

Note: transcript has occasional transcription artifacts; speaker labels are correct but minor mis-words may be present.
